Welcome to a journey that goes far beyond borders and traditions—a journey that asks us to look at what truly matters when we say goodbye. Have you ever wondered how different cultures around the globe face death, or what their rituals really say about the living? Together, we’ll explore these questions through the eyes of Caitlin Doughty, whose book, From Here to Eternity: Traveling the World to Find the Good Death, invites us to see mortality in a whole new light.
We’ll visit places where honoring the dead looks and feels completely different from what most of us might expect—from the quiet power of open-air pyres in Colorado, to the lively, colorful Day of the Dead celebrations in Mexico. Each stop on this adventure opens a window into how communities care for those they’ve lost, and how they lift up the living in the process.
As we travel with Doughty, we’ll discover the creativity, reverence, and even humor woven into these rituals. We’ll see that, while grief is universal, the ways we express it are as unique as we are. This is more than just a look at customs and ceremonies—it’s an invitation for us all to rethink what it means to say goodbye, to challenge our assumptions, and to imagine new ways to honor life’s last transition.
So, let’s explore together. What if facing death could help us live with deeper connection, healing, and even celebration? In this world of remembrance, the lines between fear and acceptance, sorrow and joy, are constantly shifting—offering us a richer, more compassionate vision of what it means to die, and, just as importantly, what it means to truly live.
